claims.statement: For every finite D, all components of the Gaussian-prime graph G_D have a finite common size bound B_D, including axis primes.
For each D >= 1, some finite set of split rational primes gives an avoiding set with no infinite self-avoiding D-step walk.
claims.source: build/main.tex thm:sieve; graph instead points to information.tex for its argument

claims.statement: A finite periodic obstruction gives the explicit uniform component bound stated in periodicity.tex, prop:periodic.
For a self-avoiding D-step segment of n steps, its diameter-width product A satisfies c n <= A <= D^2 n^2 and |E-E| >= c_D A.

For each fixed origin-centered rotated rectangle with R >= W >= 1 and RW <= P^(1-d), 0 < d < 1/4, independent fair conjugate choices over distinct split primes in [T,2T], T >= 5, have a nonzero rectangle witness with probability <= C exp(-c d^3 r) when d^3 r >= C0, for absolute positive constants.
Under exactly the rectangle lemma's hypotheses, for every r >= 1 the bad-sign probability is at most min(1, 3 exp(-d^2 r/32)); no lower threshold on d^3 r is needed.
claims.source: PROOF.md theorem (T), sections 1-6; fidelity, checker, certificate and output

claims.statement: Distinct split-prime factors are pairwise coprime; for primitive v at most one conjugate factor over each p divides v, the product of eligible norms is at most N(v), and a missing chosen factor in a nonzero witness a v forces p | a.
If d^2 r >= 1, bad sign vectors at Hamming distance <= dr/4 have collinear witnesses; each bad vector has a unique witness line.
If d^2 r >= 1, any one fixed primitive integer line has witness probability at most exp(-d^2 r/8), uniformly in its direction.
For independent fair bits B_i and real weights a_i, E exp(lambda sum_i a_i(B_i-1/2)) <= exp(lambda^2 sum_i a_i^2/8), for every real lambda.
For every real-valued 1-Lipschitz function on the uniform r-cube, E exp(lambda(f-Ef)) <= exp(r lambda^2/8) for all real lambda.
For disjoint classes S_j in the uniform r-cube at pairwise Hamming distance >= s > 0, each of mass <= m, their total mass is <= 3 max(m, exp(-s^2/(2r))). The number of classes is unrestricted.
In the asymptotic regime of geometry.tex, lem:enrichment, f_V(b)/(b L_*) >= (1 + f_Z(q)/(q L_*))/2 - O_D(g), uniformly in walks, batches, and starting laws.
Bounded time displacement gives entropy <= 2 log(n+1)+O_D(1) and the corresponding loss bound for residue entropy.
Under all conditional entropy, repetition, coverage, and parameter inequalities in coverage-transfer.tex, thm:transfer, all but fraction eta of terminal coordinates have (tau,beta)-coverage.
The schedule in schedule.tex supplies the required checkpoint entropy, future displacement bounds, and common terminal law with the stated smoothing and uniformity properties.
claims.source: build/schedule.tex, whole section; not just lem:future-shift

claims.statement: Under the full schedule hypotheses, all but eta_i of the signed prime coordinates have the checkpoint coverage in schedule.tex, prop:coverage.
Under zero avoidance, each batch has conditional information rate at least c_1/log T as stated in information.tex, prop:information-rate.
The nested common-time information costs obey the block entropy upper bound in information.tex, lem:telescope.
If finite X has at most a values, Y-dependent lists have size at most b with 1 <= b <= a, and rho is their success probability, then log a - H(X|Y) >= rho log(a/b) - h(rho).
For two joint laws on a product alphabet of size at most a and total variation epsilon <= 1/2, the conditional entropies differ by at most 2h(epsilon)+2epsilon log a.

For finite (Y,H), independently chosen signed s-coordinate subset S, mean joint residue entropy >= (1-epsilon)s Lbar and H(H) <= kappa s Lbar imply mean coordinate conditional entropy deficit <= (epsilon+kappa)Lbar, with no independence of Y and H.
